topic: SAA formation ~950 AD — post-patch verification of ISS-2695/2696/2697 (c6 holes)
our_argument_summary: WIN-023 verdict 'Unfalsifiable': the ~950 AD SAA formation date is adopted from published paleomagnetic literature (Campuzano 2019 SHAWQ2k, Tarduno 2015), not predicted; the dome links it to a preterist theological timeline with no dome-derived mechanism. Post-c6 patches: the finding no longer attributes a Schumann/aetheric-phase-transition mechanism to the dome; the window argument is now an explicit disjunction (rigorous historicist band AD 1033-1380 => clean miss; loose calendar-millennium target => base-rate-expected selection); the standardized post-hoc paragraph now separates the measured component (~950 AD date) from the dome-added theological link and scopes the no-observable claim to the latter.

verification_of_patches.ISS-2695 (c6 H0, critical — Schumann mis: FIXED. New finding reads: 'Geomagnetic excursion ~950 CE is documented in archaeomagnetic records (Campuzano 2019) — the dome correctly identifies a real paleomagnetic event, then retroactively matches it to a theological timeline...'. No Schumann, no aetheric phase transition; tracks the detail fields and the live dome site (re-confirmed this run: live wins.html WIN-023 is one line, theological match only). Residual terminology nit — see holes_found[1].
verification_of_patches.ISS-2696 (c6 H1, moderate — window-argum: SUBSTANTIALLY FIXED. The explicit disjunction landed: 'The dome's claim therefore fails on either framing: under the rigorous reading ... ~950 AD misses the target entirely; under the loose reading ... selection of one geomagnetic recurrence inside a wide opportunity window.' The former surface contradiction is resolved by scoping the two statements to different framings. Residual: the Poisson parenthetical (P ≈ 0.58–0.82) is still computed on the 347-yr historicist band but is now deployed under the LOOSE branch — see holes_found[0]. 'The window the dome implicitly constructs' is judged defensible: the dome's own label is 'full preterist timeline', and full-preterist anchoring (millennium start at resurrection ~AD 33 or AD 70) implies a little-season onset at ~1033–1070, i.e. the dome's own framing does implicitly put the target after 950.
verification_of_patches.ISS-2697 (c6 H2, moderate — no-observabl: FIXED. New paragraph opens 'The ~950 AD date itself is an empirically measured paleomagnetic result (Campuzano 2019); that part is grounded in observation. What is not empirically grounded is the theological timing link' — exactly the scoping c6 recommended. Residual one-clause phrasing nit — see holes_found[2].

holes_found.description: POISSON PARENTHETICAL STILL ON THE WRONG WINDOW (residual of c6 H1 secondary defect (a) / ISS-2696, closed): the disjunction's loose branch now reads 'Under the loose framing, combined with the ~200-400 year recurrence interval ... hitting some recurrence somewhere inside that window is more probable than not under any reasonable base-rate model (Poisson with mean recurrence 200-400 yr: P(>=1 event) ≈ 0.58-0.82).' The 0.58-0.82 figures are computed on W=347yr (the AD 1033-1380 historicist band — recomputed this run: R=200 => 0.824, R=400 => 0.580), i.e. the band the rigorous branch says the event is OUTSIDE. Under the loose framing the operative window must be wide enough to include ~950 (e.g. AD 900-1380, W≈480yr), giving P ≈ 0.70-0.91 (recomputed this run). The error is conservative — the deployed number UNDERSTATES the probability, so 'more probable than not' holds a fortiori — which is why this is minor rather than moderate. But a quantitatively careful defender can still note the parenthetical's number belongs to a window the text says the event missed.
holes_found.recommendation: Either (a) recompute the parenthetical on the loose window: '(Poisson with mean recurrence 200-400 yr on any window wide enough to include ~950 AD, e.g. AD 900-1380: P(>=1 event) ≈ 0.70-0.91)', or (b) keep the numbers and add the directional note: '(computed on the narrower historicist band; any window drawn wide enough to include ~950 AD only raises this probability)'. Option (b) is a one-clause edit. Decider note: ISS-2696 was closed; this residual is the unlanded sub-part — open a small successor rather than reopening.

holes_found.description: FINDING TERMINOLOGY: 'Geomagnetic excursion ~950 CE' — the SAA's ~950 AD emergence is a reversed-flux patch appearing at the core-mantle boundary (Campuzano 2019's term), not a geomagnetic 'excursion' in the technical paleomagnetic sense (large transient directional departures, e.g. Laschamp). Our own detail_evidence uses the correct 'reversed flux patch' language. A pedantic geophysics-literate defender could flag the summary-table term as a misnomer. Secondary style nit folded in: the finding says '~950 CE' while every other surface of this WIN (claim, detail fields, TLDRs) says '~950 AD'.
holes_found.recommendation: Replace 'Geomagnetic excursion ~950 CE is documented in archaeomagnetic records (Campuzano 2019)' with 'The emergence of the SAA's reversed-flux patch ~950 AD is documented in paleomagnetic reconstructions (Campuzano 2019)'. One-clause edit; also restores AD/CE consistency.

holes_found.description: SLIGHT OVERREACH IN THE SCOPED NO-OBSERVABLE SENTENCE: 'no measurement could distinguish a world where Satan's little season aligns with the SAA's origin from one where it does not' — strictly, date ALIGNMENT is checkable (paragraph 1 argues the dome's implied target misses ~950 under the rigorous reading); what has no observable is the CAUSAL/theological connection, not the arithmetic comparison of two dates. The surrounding sentences ('the theological connection has no observable to confirm or refute') carry the correct scoping, so the exposure is small, but the specific sentence hands a quote-miner a faint echo of the original c6 H2 tension.
holes_found.recommendation: Reword to 'no measurement could establish or refute a causal connection between the prophesied period and the SAA's origin — alignment of two dates, by itself, is not a mechanism'. One-sentence edit.

stronger_arguments.description: The full-preterist anchor actually sharpens the rigorous branch: the dome's own label is 'full preterist timeline', and full preterism dates the millennium start to the resurrection (~AD 33) or the fall of Jerusalem (AD 70), implying a little-season onset of ~AD 1033-1070 — so on the dome's OWN framing, ~950 precedes the implied target by 83-120 years. The text already contains the AD 33 => 1033 anchor; adding the AD 70 => 1070 full-preterist anchor would make the point self-contained without relying on the historicist band.

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome points at a real, peer-reviewed paleomagnetic result: the current SAA's reversed-flux patch dates to roughly 950 AD (wins.json WIN-023 detail_evidence cites Campuzano et al. 2019, doi:10.1016/j.epsl.2019.01.050, and Tarduno et al. 2015, doi:10.1038/ncomms8865 — both DOIs re-verified via the doi.org handle API this run, responseCode 1). The proximity of that date to the calendar millennium is arithmetically true (detail_verdict_text: 1000-950 = 50yr = 5%).
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Pointing at a published measurement after publication is adoption, not prediction (wins.json WIN-023 code_analysis.post_hoc=true, re-validated this run); the dome's page states the match in one line with no derivation and no registration date (raw-text/02-wins.txt WIN-023), and its live monitor.py (fetched this run, 39 domains) contains no validation domain for SAA formation. The theological anchor is non-unique (detail_verdict_text's four historicist anchors spanning AD 1033-1380), so the '5% miss' dissolves into either a clean miss of the rigorous band or a base-rate-expected hit in a loose one (detail_verdict_text disjunction, deployed via ISS-2696).

advocate_mode.best_defense: "The reviewers now concede our WIN-023 page says exactly what it says — no invented mechanism quotes this time. What remains is statistics: they admit the SAA's reversed-flux patch emerged ~950 AD and that this sits 5% from the millennium. Their Poisson number (0.58-0.82) is computed on a window they themselves say our date falls outside — if the event missed their window, the probability of a hit inside it is irrelevant to OUR claim. And their summary row calls the emergence a 'geomagnetic excursion', which no paleomagnetist would. If their statistics are deployed on the wrong window and their terminology is sloppy, the 'unfalsifiable' verdict is doing the work their math should be doing."
advocate_mode.preemptive_recommendation: The defense's only live legs are the three minor residuals above (Poisson window placement, 'excursion' terminology, alignment-vs-causation phrasing). All are one-clause edits. After them the defense collapses to 'a 5% coincidence is impressive', which the disjunction directly answers: rigorous reading => miss by 83+ years; loose reading => P(some recurrence in-window) >= 0.70.

cross_win_consistency.inconsistencies_found: The c6 cross-WIN defect (WIN-022's 'aetheric phase transition' vocabulary transplanted into WIN-023's finding) is resolved by the ISS-2695 patch — the finding no longer borrows any mechanism language. SAA-family rows (004/005/015/024) and Schumann-family rows (002/029/038) checked against the new finding: no row now claims the dome ties SAA formation timing to the Schumann cavity. No new cross-WIN tension introduced by the patches.

deeper_analysis: Verification pass on the three decider self-applied patches from the c6 review (queue item 520, class verification). All three primary holes closed: the critical Schumann misattribution is gone from the finding (the most important fix — it was the 'claims about things the dome model doesn't actually say' category on the most-read surface, with a reactive author in DM contact); the window argument now has the either/or structure that makes it airtight at the framing level; the standardized post-hoc paragraph now correctly separates the measured date from the dome-added theological link. The three residuals are all minor and all one-clause edits. The most substantive is the Poisson parenthetical: the ISS-2696 patch moved the sentence into the loose branch but kept the numbers computed on the rigorous band — the same number-vs-window mismatch c6 flagged as secondary defect (a), now smaller because the direction is conservative (0.58-0.82 understates the loose-window 0.70-0.91, so the qualitative conclusion is robust). I judged 'the window the dome implicitly constructs' acceptable rather than re-flagging it: the dome's own one-liner says 'full preterist timeline', and any full-preterist anchoring implies a target after AD 1030 — the dome's framing genuinely does implicitly construct a window that excludes 950. That reading also surfaces a stronger argument (the AD 70 => 1070 anchor) recorded above. Verdict 'Unfalsifiable' holds; recommended_action minor_edit for the three residuals.
